questions.question: Describe the stages in the formation of coal in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: About 250 to 300 million years ago, swamp forests (e.g. Glossopteris, ferns) grew and stored solar energy by photosynthesis. Dead plants fell into waterlogged swamps with little oxygen, so they did not rot completely and built up as peat. The peat was buried by layers of sand and mud. Over millions of years, pressure from the overlying layers and heat underground drove out water and changed the peat into lignite, then bituminous coal (and anthracite), forming coal seams.

questions.question: Explain how crude oil and natural gas formed and why they are found trapped under certain rocks.
questions.expected_answer: Tiny marine organisms (plankton) died and sank to the sea floor, where they were buried in mud with little oxygen. Layers of sediment buried them deeper; over millions of years heat and pressure changed the remains into crude oil and natural gas. Being lighter than water, oil and gas moved upward through porous rocks (e.g. sandstone) until trapped beneath a non-porous cap rock (e.g. shale), where they collect and can be drilled.

questions.question: Explain why fossil fuels are called stored solar energy and non-renewable resources, and give two problems caused by burning them.
questions.expected_answer: Their energy came from sunlight captured by ancient plants and algae through photosynthesis, stored as chemical energy and preserved when the remains became coal, oil and gas; burning them releases that ancient solar energy. They are non-renewable because they take millions of years to form and cannot be replaced in a human lifetime once used. Problems: carbon dioxide causes climate change; sulfur dioxide causes acid rain; smoke and ash harm health; mining damages land and water.
